lines.text: Unlike flat arrays, a tree arranges data in branching levels.

lines.fact: Every node in a tree except the root has exactly one parent
lines.text: Every node except the top has exactly one parent above it.

Any number of children, as long as there are no cycles.

lines.text: A binary search tree enforces a golden rule on every node.

lines.fact: all left descendants are smaller and all right descendants are larger
lines.text: All values in the left subtree are smaller; right subtree values are larger.
We are searching for sixty. Start at the root: fifty.

lines.fact: discarding half the remaining nodes at each step
lines.text: Sixty is greater than fifty, so discard the entire left subtree.
Now compare sixty against seventy-five: sixty is smaller, so branch left.
Found sixty after three comparisons, never touching the left subtree.

lines.fact: Inserting a node in a binary search tree follows the search path to an empty spot
lines.text: Inserting a new node follows this exact path to an empty spot.

lines.fact: Searching a balanced binary search tree takes O(log n)
lines.text: Halving remaining candidates at each branch gives lightning-fast O(log n) search.

lines.fact: height becomes n and search takes O(n)
lines.text: Beware: insert in sorted order and the tree becomes a skewed line taking O(n).

quiz.q: Why does searching a balanced binary search tree take O(log n) time?
options: It checks nodes level by level starting from leaves.
It discards half the remaining nodes at each step.
All nodes are stored in contiguous array memory.
quiz.fact: Searching a balanced binary search tree takes O(log n) time by discarding half the remaining nodes at each step.

lines.text: Can we read every value out of this tree in sorted order?

lines.fact: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, current node, then right subtree
lines.text: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, current node, then right subtree.
Descend all the way left to ten first, and visit ten.
Backtrack to twenty, then visit twenty's right child, thirty.
Next visit root forty, then cross into the right subtree.
Visit fifty, sixty, then seventy to complete the full traversal.
Reading in that exact sequence gives ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy.

lines.fact: produces values in sorted ascending order
lines.text: Inorder traversal of a binary search tree produces values in sorted ascending order.

lines.fact: Inorder traversal visits all n nodes in O(n) time
lines.text: Every one of the n nodes is visited exactly once in O(n) time.

quiz.q: What is the result of performing an inorder traversal on a binary search tree?
options: Nodes are visited in reverse insertion order.
Values are produced in sorted ascending order.
Values are grouped level by level from root to leaves.
quiz.fact: An inorder traversal of a binary search tree produces values in sorted ascending order.
